question.problem: Find the set of values of $x$ that satisfy $3x+5>14$ or $2x-3\le 1.$ Express your answer in interval notation.
question.worked_solution:
We start by solving $3x+5>14:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3x+5 & >14 \\ 3x & >9 \\ x & >3\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196049/assets/5dca213f8266a9bd001380b30368e5996b24fa2ddb6d3aef5670befde451e77d.png)

Then, we solve $2x-3\le 1:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-3 & \le 1 \\ 2x & \le 4 \\ x & \le 2\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196049/assets/454e1de1e32bb5e3fb03dc280076414493d9e4a9c042246be565d8550c2012f2.png)

To graph the values of $x$ that satisfy either inequality, we overlay the two graphs on the same number line:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14196049/assets/531c59b67623a10db6af4236187e7d50315e7068585d6a5e6882db0d1997bdce.png)

Therefore, the final solution is $x\le 2$ or $x>3.$ We can write this using interval notation as

$$
(-\infty ,2]\cup (3,\infty ).\,
$$
